TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate.rationale: The phase loss this entry recorded is gone. C# runs Hook.ModifyEnergyCostInCombat as two complete listener passes -- every TryModifyEnergyCostInCombat (Hook.cs:1580-1583) and then every TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate (Hook.cs:1584-1587) -- and Corruption is in the second (CorruptionPower.cs:16). The sim now reproduces exactly that: HookSystem._each (sts2_rl/hooks.py:153-180) re-walks the ordered listener list once per suffix in _PHASES order (hooks.py:36), HookSystem.modify_card_energy_cost (hooks.py:391-395) is a _each consumer, and CorruptionPower declares `modify_card_energy_cost_late` (powers.py:648) rather than the plain method, so its hard 0 lands strictly after every plain-pass modifier (relics/spiked_gauntlets.py:26-31, and the ported Curious/Tangled powers) regardless of registration or acquisition order -- confirmed by execution (`_phase_hooks(CorruptionPower)` == {'modify_card_energy_cost'}, cost 0 in both application orders) and by test/test_hook_order.py's passing energy-cost order tests.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: PHASE LOSS. This is a phase-suffixed C# hook and the sim has a single unphased dispatch, which is hook_dispatch gap G3 (24 dispatchers lose their phase structure; 27 phase-suffixed hooks declared on AbstractModel). Per binding rule 3 the mechanism keeps G3's `gap` verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Corruption is a LATE-phase cost modifier: C# runs it in Hook.ModifyEnergyCostInCombat's second pass (TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate, CorruptionPower.cs:16-25), strictly after every early-phase modifier. The sim's single modify_card_energy_cost pass orders it by registration instead, so Corruption contends with the ported early-phase modifiers -- Curious (powers.py:2883) and Spiked Gauntlets -- by accident of application order. Corruption returning a hard 0 makes it order-sensitive in the worst way: it must WIN over Spiked Gauntlets' +1, and it does so only if it happens to be registered later. Same shape as hook_dispatch G3's own executed Tangled/Free-Attack witness.

ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition.issue: SETTLED 2026-07-30 (round 11), by execution -- PREMISE CHECKED per PROMPT.md class 12, and the entry's inherited (i) sub-claim was WRONG; a different, real pairing replaces it. The destination-pile DECISION is genuinely replaced by an after-the-fact move: C# (CorruptionPower.cs:27-38) returns (PileType.Exhaust, position) from the ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition chain -- unconditionally, ignoring the chain's incoming pileType, whenever card.Type==Skill -- so a played Skill never enters the discard pile at all. The sim lets combat._resolve_card_play append the card to the discard pile (combat.py:812-814), compute (but not yet apply) the modify_card_play_result_pile chain (combat.py:842), run the play loop, and only inside on_card_played (combat.py:904, fired from CorruptionPower.on_card_played, powers.py:799-810) does Corruption pull the card out of the discard pile and append it to the exhaust pile, firing on_card_exhausted itself. STALE, EXECUTED, CORRECTED: the entry's (i) claimed Nostalgia (powers.py:4132-4163, its own modify_card_play_result_pile) beats Corruption and blocks the exhaust. `.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/power-5-corruption-nostalgia-contention.py` -- Corruption(1) + Nostalgia(1) on the player, play a Defend (Skill) -- lands the card in exhaust_pile, NOT draw_pile: Corruption wins, contradicting the old text. Reading NostalgiaPower.cs alongside CorruptionPower.cs shows why, on the C# side too: Nostalgia's chain override only fires `if (pileType != PileType.Discard)` -- i.e. only if nothing has redirected it yet -- while Corruption's override ignores the incoming pileType entirely and always forces Exhaust for a Skill. So in C#, Corruption beats Nostalgia REGARDLESS OF LISTENER ORDER (not merely 'last writer wins' as the old text framed it), and the sim's after-the-fact `card in player.discard_pile` test happens to reach the same answer today because Corruption's on_card_played (line 904, inside the play loop) always runs before Nostalgia's post-loop draw_top move (combat.py:929-931) -- coincidentally right, not order-safe. THE REAL LIVE PAIRING is Rebound, not Nostalgia: ReboundPower.cs has the IDENTICAL 'only if still Discard' guard as Nostalgia (`if (pileType != PileType.Discard) return`), so C# ALSO always has Corruption beat Rebound, order-free -- but the sim's ReboundPower (powers.py:3220-3246) does NOT implement modify_card_play_result_pile at all; like Corruption, it is ALSO an after-the-fact on_card_played mover, testing the SAME `card in player.discard_pile` membership Corruption tests. Two after-the-fact movers racing on one shared membership test ARE genuinely order-dependent, unlike the hook-chain's incoming-pileType-based arbitration. EXECUTED (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/power-5-corruption-rebound-order.py`): Corruption applied before Rebound -> played Skill lands in exhaust_pile (matches C#); Rebound applied before Corruption -> the SAME played Skill lands on TOP OF THE DRAW PILE instead (`draw_top`), diverging from C#, which always exhausts it regardless of which power the player picked up first. TRIGGER: CorruptionPower (powers.py:780-810, the Corruption card) and ReboundPower (powers.py:3220-3246, the Rebound card) are both real ported Ironclad-pool card powers with no acquisition-order constraint between them; any run picking up Rebound before Corruption and later playing a Skill while both are active hits this. FIX: give CorruptionPower a real `modify_card_play_result_pile` override that forces the pile to a value the sim's exhaust-keyword mechanism recognizes BEFORE the play loop (matching C#'s chain timing, combat.py:842), rather than an after-the-fact on_card_played move -- which requires widening the sim's hook (currently narrowed to 'discard'/'draw_top' only, hooks.py:604-613, with real exhaust handled by a wholly separate keyword path at combat.py:846) to also carry an unconditional-override 'exhaust' outcome, since neither of the sim's two existing pile-decision mechanisms (the discard/draw_top hook, and the exhausts_this_play keyword flag) currently has a slot for a power-driven, unconditional, incoming-state-ignoring redirect. RADIUS: ReboundPower's own on_card_played (same after-the-fact-mover shape, same fix needed to move it onto the pre-loop hook) and the exhaust-keyword branch's interaction with a widened hook (combat.py:846, 921-924). EVENT-TIMING half of the original text (Feel No Pain / Dark Embrace seeing on_card_exhausted fire mid-on_card_played rather than after the whole card resolves) is a real, structurally-guaranteed secondary consequence of the same after-the-fact-mover shape, not independently re-verified to a concrete divergent outcome this pass -- carried as part of the same fix's radius, not a separately demonstrated live edge.
